title: Delegation isolated worktrees are never removed: hundreds of stale checkouts under ~/.termal/delegations and stale git worktree registrations
outcome: Reported by Greg 2026-09-02 ('we must stop creating mysterious workspaces outside the main directory'). Facts (read-only): ~/.termal/delegations holds 317 delegation directories, each with a worktree/ git checkout; git worktree list in the TermAl repo still registers 4 of them (delegation-508d5446 -> session-1544, delegation-726fe542 -> session-1352, delegation-c72676fe -> session-1388, delegation-e7305cd4 -> session-1545; all long-finished reviewer delegations at old commits eab8ed4/7cdb08b), the rest are orphaned directories whose registrations were pruned. Code: prepare_isolated_delegation_worktree (delegations.rs) creates a git worktree for DelegationWritePolicy::IsolatedWorktree under ~/.termal/delegations/<id>/worktree; IsolatedWorktreeCleanupGuard only removes it when CREATION fails (guard is disarmed on success at delegations.rs:657); nothing removes the worktree when the delegation completes, fails, is canceled, or when the child session/delegation record is removed, and there is no boot-time sweep. Expected: (1) on terminal delegation cleanup (the same path that tears down the child runtime, publish_delegation_refresh_side_effects / remove_delegation_child_session) remove the isolated worktree when it carries no uncommitted changes (reviewer/read-only children always; writer children once their patch has been consumed or the delegation record is removed) via git worktree remove --force + prune, and record the removal on the delegation; (2) never delete a worktree with uncommitted changes silently — keep it and surface it (delegation note / operator warning) so a writer's deliverable is not lost; (3) a boot-time sweep that prunes registrations and directories whose delegation record no longer exists, with the same dirty-tree guard and a log line per removal; (4) docs/features/agent-delegation-sessions.md documents the lifecycle. Also review whether reviewer (read-only) delegations should ever get a worktree at all. Standing rule recorded in bd memory no-worktrees-outside-main covers agent-created worktrees; this bead covers TermAl-created ones. No Beads IDs in code comments.
acceptance: Isolated delegation worktrees are cleaned through the existing lifecycle only after their runtime/turn/admission users have released them; dirty or unconsumed writer data and uncertain ownership are retained with an observable reason; follow-up remains usable.
A bounded post-inventory startup sweep removes eligible managed orphan/terminal roots and their Git registrations using the same rules, without touching unrelated or live worktrees.

Cleanup and its tests never follow a symlink/junction outside the validated delegation root; tests use only owned temporary roots; and default delegation storage derives from AppState persistence while resolving, for the production host, to the same delegation directory as before this change, so existing roots stay recognised as managed.
Deterministic lifecycle/path/refusal tests and the standard review pair are complete, and the lifecycle is documented. The full landing gate remains integration-owned.
